blockHints.station_type: Type of ortho station (clinical, communication, prioritisation)
blockHints.clinical_scenario: High-level scenario text shown to the candidate, e.g. 'Your consultant has requested you to organise the trauma list for the following day...'
blockHints.background_overview: Background context combining theatre and patient information in prose. Example: 'You are in an MTC with allied specialties available. There is a CEPOD list overnight; XR is available only on the full-day list. All patients are in hospital, consented, marked and swabbed. Patient #6 awaits USS to confirm collection.'
blockHints.examiner_additional_info: Parallel list with expanded details/bullets per patient number
blockHints.suggested_order_overview: Short overview introducing the management rationale before the detailed list order. Example: 'Prioritise septic and time-critical cases first, align NOF THA within BOAST timelines on the hip list, and schedule cases requiring XR on the full-day list. Manage diabetic optimization and imaging dependencies in parallel.'
blockHints.suggested_order: Recommended ordering across CEPOD, full-day list, and half-day list with brief justifications
blockHints.interview_questions:
Q&A pairs to probe candidate's prioritisation reasoning. Common questions: 1. 'How would you prioritise these patients?' 2. 'Why would you put patient X first/on the CEPOD list?' 3. 'What factors influenced your decision?' 4. 'How does BOAST guidance affect your list order?' 5. 'What would you do if XR wasn't available on the full-day list?' 6. 'How would you manage the diabetic patient's optimization?' 
Answers should reference: guidelines (BOAST, NICE, BPT), time targets (<24h, <36h), clinical priorities (sepsis, NV compromise), resource constraints (XR, specialist surgeon)
blockHints.approved: Whether this station has been approved for use
